# Learnings and mistakes

No structural facts are generated for this page; the store has no concept of a mistake, only of records, decisions and handovers. Everything here is written by hand.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
MISTAKE, mine, worst of the session: the local runner could post a green status
for a battery that never finished. The command loop was fed by a heredoc, so
every gate command inherited the remaining command list as its stdin; any
command reading stdin swallowed the rest, the loop ended with no failure
recorded, and the verdict never checked that all 52 ran. Reproduced: the old
shape ran 3 of 4 and reported no failure. Fixed with < /dev/null plus an
explicit RAN equals TOTAL assertion, 12fa46b. I had already told the founder
the guardrails were sound before this was found.

MISTAKE, mine, security: the runner parsed its battery from the CHECKED-OUT
workflow, and its filter admits any line starting with sh. A fork pull request
could add sh -c to the gates job and have it run through eval with the
founder's full user. Fixed by reading the list from origin/main.

MISTAKE, mine, honesty: docs/LOCAL-VERIFICATION.md claimed the retained
workflows were workflow_dispatch only and ubuntu only. Written without
checking, and false. Corrected in place at d018c55.

MISTAKE, mine: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR isolates settings but NOT plugin installs, so
runs described as throwaway installed into the real user scope and shadowed
both development clones. The bulk uninstall that followed fixed one product and
regressed the other by about forty releases.

NEAR MISS: git push --dry-run printed the ref update and exited 0; the real push
was rejected for five required checks. A dry run stops before the ref update,
which is where protection is evaluated.

LEARNING: load average reached 187 and a battery documented at 8 to 13 minutes
ran past 45. Measurements taken under that load are not evidence.
<!-- bm-human:end -->
